We release LiveBench, the
                                                  first benchmark that (1) contains frequently-updated questions from recent information
                                                  sources, (2) scores answers automatically according to objective ground-truth values
Abacus.AI, 2 NYU, 3 Nvidia, 4 UMD, 5 USC, 6 Columbia
Colin White∗ 1 , Samuel Dooley∗1 , Manley Roberts∗1 , Arka Pal∗1 , Benjamin Feuer2

LiveBench questions are difficult: no
current model achieves higher than 70% accuracy.

If the LLM has seen the questions of a benchmark
                                         during training, its performance on that benchmark will be artificially inflated

LiveBench currently consists of 18 tasks across 6 categories: math, coding,
reasoning, language, instruction following, and data analysis.

Each task is designed to have 40-100 questions which span a range of difficulty, from easy to very
challenging, while loosely aiming for an overall 30-70% success rate on the top models for each
task.

In each update, we replace 1/6 of the questions on average,
so that the benchmark is fully refreshed roughly every 6 months.

Each month, we do not release
the new questions until one month later, so that the public leaderboard always has 1/6 questions that
are private.

We choose tasks to update based primarily on two factors: (1) the oldest tasks, and (2)
the currently easiest tasks.

For all models and tasks, we perform single-turn evaluation with temperature 0, unless otherwise
noted in the model card.
we compute the final LiveBench score as the average of all six categories

the median and mean average scores (among models
included in all iterations of the leaderboard) have both dropped by about 1.2%
Claude-3-Opus      GPT-4-Turbo           0.388            0.103          0.294             0.460

LiveBench makes use of automatic regex-based grading methods in order to avoid the biases and other
downsides of LLM judging

our grading methodology is designed to be fully permissive, accommodating all answer
formats within reason

we do not
publicly release any of the code used to generate LiveBench questions, we always modify the
generating code when updating the LiveBench questions (making the questions harder)
Therefore, a limited fraction of LiveBench is likely contaminated on all recent LLMs.

we hope to add non-English
language tasks in the future

while ground truth scoring is beneficial in many ways, it
still cannot be used for certain use cases

The board has seven suites. Five are agentic: the model works through real end-to-end tasks with tools (plans, edits files, drives apps, runs code) and produces a result that is graded automatically.

**Browser Use**25Complete multi-step jobs in working web applications, through a real browser that the model sees by screenshot.
**Data Analysis**150 questionsShort data-analysis questions on small tables, each with a single correct answer. Not agentic: no tools, one answer per question.
**Research**22Answer an open-ended brief by researching it and writing a report with sources.
**Design**25Produce or rework a finished document to a brief: Word documents, PDFs and slide decks.

LiveBench currently contains a set of 18 diverse tasks across 6 categories, and we will release new, harder tasks over time.
Each question has verifiable, objective ground-truth answers, allowing hard questions to be scored accurately and automatically, without the use of an LLM judge.
LiveBench appeared as a [Spotlight Paper](https://openreview.net/forum?id=sKYHBTAxVa) in ICLR 2025.
Also available are the [model answers](https://huggingface.co/datasets/livebench/model_answer) and the [model judgments](https://huggingface.co/datasets/livebench/model_judgment).
The current LiveBench release is 2025-04-25; however, not all questions for this release are public on Huggingface.
Today, we release the initial batch of 960 questions and plan to release sets of questions every month.

Removed house traversal task. We discovered ambiguity in the parsing of the answers, and upon fixing it, some models achieved 100% on the task.
This brought the total number of questions to 1000, and all future updates add and remove the same number, to stay at 1000 total questions.
The cta task has been retired.
This update introduces a new agentic coding category, where models must operate in a multi-turn, realistic development environment to resolve issues from real Github repositories.
